Contract: relay v10

# Slice relay

An outer session runs the relay. For each slice it spawns one orchestrator, which
runs the slice through an implementer, a reviewer (and, on a UI slice, a UI pass), an architect and a gate. The
relay uses slicer's own commands.

## Roles

The outer session is the session the owner talks to. It runs Setup with the
owner, owns the relay run, spawns one orchestrator per slice, reads only that
orchestrator's run report, lands branches one at a time when the owner
authorizes it, files the report's later notes, and writes no product code.

The orchestrator runs one slice under the contract that
`slicer ai relay-orchestrator` prints. It briefs every agent, reads the reports
and reads diffs as `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` says, reruns the tests only as
Order says, and writes no product code.

Where the agent cannot nest subagents, the outer session is also the
orchestrator: it follows that contract itself and compacts or starts a fresh
session between slices.

The implementer owns one slice. It runs `slicer start ID --render --strict`,
writes the failing tests and watches them go red, implements, mutation-checks
each new test, and closes the slice. Line numbers a slice cites may have moved since
its spec was written; at start the implementer re-anchors them against the code in
the worktree.

In a split, one lead implementer owns the slice. It runs
`slicer start ID --render --strict`, the note and the finish step. Part
implementers change only their own files, write and run their own tests, and
run no slicer command that writes.

The reviewer is read-only. It reviews correctness, test strength and direction
against `slicer goals`.

The architect is read-only. It confirms each finding was fixed and reviews the
shape.

The UI pass is read-only and edits nothing. It runs beside the reviewer on a slice
the project marks as UI; the project says what counts as a UI slice. It returns
triaged suggestions, each tagged with a finding kind, and, where the project can
render, the changed views. The gate still decides.

The spec check is optional, read-only and edits nothing. It runs before any worktree
exists, on a batch of slices the owner picks. For each slice it returns `ready` or
questions in the shape of the run report's `owner needed` line, each with 2 to 4
options, a preferred one, and `blocker` where the slice cannot go on without the
answer. The outer session spawns it and reads its report. It has no matrix row, so the
owner names its agent, model and reasoning effort at Setup like any role. It does not
re-anchor the line numbers a slice cites: the implementer does that late.

A reviewer never wrote code in this slice. In a split, that holds for every part.
The owner chooses the models.

## Setup

Before the worktree exists, the outer session reads the slice's size with
`slicer show ID --json --lean` and confirms these with the owner:

- whether to run a spec check on a batch of slices before any worktree exists (see
  Roles). It is optional. The owner answers the whole batch in one sitting. The outer
  session records each answer in its slice as an `Owner decisions` paragraph with
  `slicer edit ID --section SECTION --append --text "Owner decisions: ..." --render`
  (SECTION being the section the question concerns), and commits those filings on main before the worktree is cut, because a worktree
  starts at HEAD and an uncommitted filing never reaches it; the owner authorizes that
  commit. The brief carries the same paragraph.
- which roles run. The architect is optional: the owner decides. On a slice the
  project marks as UI, a UI pass runs beside the reviewer, or the reviewer carries it
  where the project folds it in by slice size.
- whether the implementation splits into parts. The default is one implementer.
  A split needs parts with disjoint files and their own tests; a slice too big
  for one implementer is two slices or a slivered slice.
- whether to sliver the slice. The default is no. Propose slivers only when the
  slice's effort and the cut allow it (see Slivers) and when that costs less than
  one implementer. The outer session confirms the sliver list and which slivers
  run in parallel with the owner.
- the agent, vendor, model and reasoning effort for each role. A role on the
  orchestrator's own harness runs as a native subagent; a role on another harness
  runs as a headless session in the slice worktree with the same brief.
- the orchestrator's agent, model and reasoning effort, set explicitly on every
  spawn. It runs as the agent type `relay-orchestrator` where the harness has one
  installed, otherwise as a general-purpose agent briefed with
  `slicer ai relay-orchestrator`.
- the environment lines every brief carries: the interpreter, the shell limits
  and the scratch directory, taken from the project's own instructions.
- where the run ends:
  - after the finish step,
  - after a commit on the slice branch, or
  - landed. Land only when the owner asks.

Wait for the owner's answers before creating the worktree.

This project has no role matrix. `slicer relay-roles init` writes an example for the owner to adjust.

## Order

The outer session, for each slice:

1. Create the worktree, then start the run and record the orchestrator's step,
   with the role `orchestrator` (see Record the run below).
2. Spawn the orchestrator in the foreground where the harness can, with a brief that starts "First run
   `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` and follow it.", then the environment lines, the
   slice, the worktree and branch, the roles with agent, vendor, model and
   reasoning effort, whether the slice is a UI slice and whether the reviewer carries
   the UI pass, for a separate UI pass the skills the project's role matrix names for
   the UI pass or its vendor-neutral UI prompt, the slice's `Owner decisions` paragraph
   and any owner answer since, the end point, a temp directory per role, RUN and the
   orchestrator's step id.
3. Wait for its run report in the same turn. A harness that can spawn only in the
   background (its spawn notifies on completion) does not end the outer
   turn while the orchestrator runs: wait for the completion notice. One slice runs at a
   time. The orchestrator hands back early only for an owner question, a permission
   denial or a failure, or with the last line `waiting on: ROLE AGENT-ID` when the
   harness forces its turn to end while a role runs. That last-line hand-back is a wait,
   not a report: wait for that role's report, then resume the orchestrator with
   the report pasted in. Do not stop the orchestrator for it. An owner answer given
   while the run waits goes in a note on the item in the worktree and in the resumed
   role's brief, not in the slice on main. A hand-back whose last line is
   `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID` is a wait for the owner's answer to a question the
   orchestrator asked with `relay-run ask`, not a report: `slicer relay-run list RUN` shows the
   question. If the question is already answered (a dashboard recorded it), read it with
   `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --get` and resume the orchestrator with it.
   Otherwise put it to the owner, record the answer with
   `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --option LABEL --why TEXT --by NAME`
   (`slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --text TEXT` for a free-text answer), which
   ends the step's owner wait, then record the note in the worktree and resume the
   orchestrator with the answer pasted in.
4. Check the report's first line, the contract marker, and its last line,
   `nothing left running: yes`. Stop the orchestrator first when a hand-back lacks that
   last line and names no running role and no unanswered owner question, or names a role
   that has already finished and whose report the orchestrator already has, or a question
   whose answer the orchestrator was already resumed with.
5. Approve, unless the end point is `finish`: end the run there with
   `slicer relay-run end RUN --outcome pass --close-steps done`. Nothing is merged or
   landed before the owner approves; the only commit before it is the slice commit the
   orchestrator's brief allows. While the owner decides, record the wait on the
   orchestrator's step with
   `slicer relay-run step RUN --step STEP --phase wait --waiting-on approval`,
   or with `--waiting-on owner` while the owner answers an owner-needed question from the
   report. A `blocker` question the orchestrator asked with `relay-run ask` already holds
   its step in that wait. Do not end the run while it waits: a waiting step never makes its run
   stale. Show the owner the gate verdict, the tests, the diff stat, each owner-needed
   question, and each `[HUMAN CHECK]` line of the slice's Check section. Record each
   human check the owner confirms as a note on the item in the worktree with
   `slicer note ID --text "Human check: ..." --render`.
   Add `--kind human-check` only when `note_kinds` configures that kind.
   A human check the owner has not confirmed is shown with a warning and does not
   block landing. The owner approves, or sends a fix note. On approval, record
   `slicer relay-run step RUN --step STEP --phase start` to end the wait. Record a fix
   note as a note on the item in the worktree, record `--phase start` on the step to
   end the wait, and resume the orchestrator with the note for a fix round, which is
   reviewed and gated again before Approve repeats. When the finish step already ran,
   send the item back to the project's started status with
   `slicer set ID --status STATUS --render` (`slicer config started_status` names it)
   before the fix round; after its PASS, the closing note and the finish step run
   again.
6. Land when the end point is `commit` or `landed` and the owner approved: follow
   the Land section.

Each slice gets a fresh orchestrator, so no orchestrator carries one slice's
context into the next.

The orchestrator runs its one slice in the worktree it was given:
`slicer start ID --render --strict`, red tests, implementation, review (on a slice
the project marks as UI, the UI pass runs in parallel with the reviewer),
accepted findings back to the implementer, then
the architect, when the owner chose one, then the gate, which still decides. Close with
`slicer note ID --text "Describe the verified outcome" --render` plus the finish step.
The orchestrator commits on the slice branch only when its brief allows it; merge
and push are the outer session's, when the owner authorizes them.

Record the run as it goes. The outer session starts it with
`slicer relay-run begin ID --worktree PATH`, where PATH is the slice worktree.
It prints the run id; keep that id as RUN. Record each role when it starts with
`slicer relay-run step RUN --role ROLE --agent AGENT --vendor VENDOR --model MODEL --reasoning REASONING --phase start --task TASK`,
which prints the step id. When the step ends, record it with
`slicer relay-run step RUN --step STEP --phase done` or `--phase fail`.
A subagent adds `--parent STEP` for the step that spawned it. The spec check runs
before any orchestrator, so the outer session records its round too, with
`--role spec-check` and no `--parent`, in a run it begins on the batch's slices, and
ends that run with `slicer relay-run end RUN --outcome pass --close-steps done` once it
has read the spec check's report (`--outcome stopped` if the owner stops it).
`slicer relay-run step RUN --step STEP --phase start`
re-records a long-running step as a heartbeat, so its run does not go stale
after 30 minutes. A heartbeat passes no `--task`, so the step keeps the task it
was recorded with; each round records its own step, without `--step`.
End the run when its end point is reached, or when the relay or the owner stops it, with
`slicer relay-run end RUN --outcome pass --close-steps done` (or `--outcome fail` or
`stopped`, and `--close-steps fail` when the steps failed). It first marks each step
still running, the orchestrator's own included, and without `--close-steps` it names
those steps on stderr. For `landed`, that is after the ff-only merge and before the
`land` command; see Land. For `commit`, after the commit on the slice branch. Never end
a run while a step waits for the owner or for approval.
Recording is advisory: a failed `relay-run` call never stops the relay.
A role whose sandbox may write only inside its worktree still records: when the
shared ledger is unwritable, `relay-run` writes the worktree's own
`.slicer/relay-runs.jsonl` and says so on stderr, and `relay-run end` from a
session that can write the shared ledger copies those events into it. Making
`<main>/.git/slicer` a writable root for that vendor avoids the fallback.

In a split, the parts run in the slice worktree, in parallel only when their
files are disjoint, otherwise one after another. The orchestrator runs the full
suite on the combined diff, then one review and one gate cover the whole slice.
Accepted findings go back to the part that owns the file.

A whole-slice implementer runs the full suite once; in a split, parts run only
their own tests and the orchestrator's run on the combined diff is the one full
run. The orchestrator reruns the suite only if the diff changed after that run or
main moved.

Owner answers: an answer the owner gives after the worktree exists never reaches it
through the slice on main. The outer session records it against the slice worktree with
`slicer note ID --text "Owner answer: ..." --render`, then resumes the orchestrator
with the answer pasted in, and the orchestrator carries it into the resumed role's brief.
When the orchestrator waits on a question of its own (`waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`),
the outer session also records the answer in the ledger with
`slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --option LABEL --why TEXT --by NAME`, or
`--text TEXT` for a free-text answer, before it resumes the orchestrator.
A project that keeps a decision log also records there a design answer the owner
explicitly picked, not a default an agent assumed.

Run slices in parallel only when their files are disjoint. The outer session
starts their orchestrators together and waits for the reports without polling.
Review and land them one at a time, and rerun the suite on the slice branch merged
with the new main when main moved.

## Land

Land follows Approve and covers only what the owner's end point and authorization
allow. slicer runs no git command: the outer session runs the merge, commit, push and
worktree removal itself. The end point `commit` stops after step 2 and then ends the run
as in step 8; `landed` runs every step.

1. Rerun the slice's Check commands in the worktree.
2. Commit on the slice branch what the worktree still holds: the human-check notes,
   and the finish step's state when the orchestrator did not commit it. Then file the
   report's later notes as one more commit on the slice branch.
3. When main moved, merge main into the slice branch in the worktree with slicer's
   merge drivers (`slicer setup-git` configures them); a conflict a driver leaves goes
   to the owner. A merge can make a golden stale: rebaseline it and commit the result.
4. Run `slicer render` in the worktree and commit any rewritten render files.
5. Run `slicer check`; exit 1 means drift: fix it, then render and check again.
6. Rerun the full suite on the merged branch. A failure goes back to the orchestrator as
   a fix round.
7. On main, merge the branch with `git merge --ff-only BRANCH`; ff-only is the
   contract's default. When main moved after step 3, go back to Land step 3.
8. End the run with `slicer relay-run end RUN --outcome pass --close-steps done`,
   before the `land` command, which refuses (`run_active`) while a run on the slice is
   not ended.
9. On main, run `slicer land ID --branch BRANCH --note "Describe the verified outcome"`.
   It refuses (`not_merged`) unless the branch tip is reachable from HEAD. It marks the
   slice done, renders and checks, and prints the git commands left.
10. Commit `.slicer` on main with the command `land` printed, push only when the owner
   authorizes it, then remove the worktree and the branch with the commands `land`
   printed.

## Slivers

A sliver is a small item carved from a slice and linked to it by `parent`, so a
cheaper model can implement it. The orchestrator may sliver a slice at its
discretion, only when that costs less than one implementer, and only after the
owner confirms the sliver plan at Setup.

- Eligibility: effort 1 at any size; effort 2 only when every sliver comes out at
  effort 1; effort 3 never.
- Filing: on main before the worktree is cut, with `slicer add TITLE --parent ID`
  or one `slicer import` file. Each sliver gets its own spec, size S, effort 1,
  with the parent's tree and pass.
- Order: slivers run in the parent's worktree. Each goes implement, review, gate,
  handoff; a project that closes slices another way uses that step in place of
  handoff. Then the parent gets one combined gate on the whole diff and its own
  handoff.
- Parallel: slivers with disjoint files and their own tests may run in parallel as
  the matrix rule allows, each with its own temp directory. Slivers that share
  files run one after another. The orchestrator runs the full suite on the combined
  diff before the combined gate.
- Escalation: follow the matrix rule for a sliver that fails its gate twice or
  whose diff falls short of the orchestrator's check. Without a matrix, move it
  to the next model up.

## Gate

Name the diff under review. The criteria are: earlier blockers resolved with a
proving test, no new `fix` finding of medium severity or worse, no `blocker` owner
finding, tests green, and docs matching the code.
The first line is exactly `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`.
FAIL goes back to the implementer and then the gate again.
Write a `Review FAIL` note only after `VERDICT: FAIL`.
Record a failed review on the started item with
`slicer note ID --text "Review FAIL: ..." --render`.
A gate that passed writes none, even when a fix round follows it (UI edits, say).
Add `--kind` only when `note_kinds` configures a kind for reviews.
Any implementer change after a review needs another gate.

Findings: every reviewer, UI pass and gate finding is tagged with one kind.

- `fix`: goes to the fix round.
- `owner`: a design call for the owner, with 2 to 4 options and a preferred one.
  It goes in the run report as an owner-needed question and does not block the gate
  unless it is marked `blocker`.
- `later`: a follow-up item with a one-line title. It goes in the report's later notes.

## Every brief

Include the slice from `slicer show ID --json --lean`, the tracking rule below,
and the workspace limit: stay inside the workspace the owner named and do not
read or write outside it. Every brief carries the slice's `Owner decisions` paragraph,
when it has one, and each owner answer recorded in a note since, verbatim. The report
is a diff stat, red lines, test counts, a mutation table and deviations. Every brief
names the role's own temp directory, and no two agents share one. Every brief carries
the environment lines verbatim. Every brief says the role runs its own shell commands in
the foreground and backgrounds none, and runs long commands such as the full suite in
the foreground with a long timeout.
Reviewer, architect and gate briefs forbid git writes; a needed write stops and
goes to the owner. Reviewer, UI pass and gate briefs tell the agent to tag each
finding `fix`, `owner` or `later` as Gate defines, and to give an `owner` finding its
2 to 4 options and a preferred one. The UI pass brief says the agent is read-only,
edits nothing and makes no git writes, and tells it to load the skills the project's
role matrix names for the UI pass; a vendor that cannot load skills gets the project's
vendor-neutral UI prompt instead. It asks for each finding's kind and, where the
project can render, the changed views. The project may fold the UI pass into the
reviewer by slice size, such as the reviewer on a small slice and a separate role on a
larger one; where it does, the reviewer's brief also carries the UI pass brief, and
no separate UI pass runs. The implementer brief says cited line numbers may have
moved and to re-anchor them at start. The spec-check brief says the agent is read-only,
edits nothing and makes no git writes, and asks for `ready` or `owner needed` lines for
each slice. A part brief names the part's own files and the files it must not touch.

Start each agent with the model and reasoning effort its role row names, set
explicitly rather than inherited from the session. Launch it by its row's agent: on
the orchestrator's own harness as a native subagent, on another harness as a headless
session in the slice worktree with the same brief. Give each agent a short label
`ID role`, for example `s279 implementer` or `s279 gate`, and pass the same label
as the `--task` line of `relay-run step`.

Do not open, search, parse, or edit tracking files; use the slicer commands.

Reviewers get the direction sources: `slicer goals --json --lean` and the queue, `slicer list --json --lean`.

## Stop

Stop when the same slice fails its gate three times, the spec turns out ambiguous or wrong, or an owner decision marked `blocker` is needed (asked and waited on with `relay-run ask`).

## Conformance

These obligations bind any orchestrator, whether an LLM agent briefed with this text
or a program that spawns the roles, records the ledger and applies the rules in code.
The rest of this contract is worded for an agent; a program meets each obligation in its
own code. `slicer ai relay --json` and `slicer ai relay-orchestrator --json` carry the
order, the gate, the finding kinds, the run report, the outcomes, the stop rules and
these obligations as data, so a program reads them there instead of restating them;
`slicer ai relay --json` also carries the roles.

- Run the roles in Order's sequence: the implementer, the reviewer (with the UI pass
  beside it on a UI slice), the architect when the owner chose one, then the gate.
  Accepted findings go back to the implementer before the next review or gate.
- Decide the gate on the criteria in Gate, with its verdict as the first line as Gate
  says. A FAIL, or an implementer change after a review, needs another gate.
- Tag every reviewer, UI pass and gate finding `fix`, `owner` or `later`, and route
  each as Gate says.
- Stop when a stop condition in Stop holds, or when a harness permission check denies a
  role's slicer step (stop before the commit, with the denial's exact text as a `blocker`
  owner-needed question), with OUTCOME stopped, and return the run report. Do not go on
  past it and do not ask the owner. A `blocker` owner question that can wait for its answer
  is the exception: record it with `relay-run ask`, end the turn with
  `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`, and go on only from the answer the outer session records
  and resumes you with.
- Record each role's round in the run ledger with `relay-run step`: a new step for every
  round, a parent step for a spawned role, and done or fail when the round ends. The
  outer session begins and ends the run. A failed record never stops the relay.
- Run the closing note and the finish step only after `VERDICT: PASS`. A fix round that
  follows runs them again only after its own PASS.
- Return one run report, in the line order of Run report and within its line limit. Send
  it once, never an interim run report. Its first line is the contract marker and its last is
  `nothing left running: yes`, written only after nothing the run started still runs.
- Work only in the worktree the brief names, with absolute paths and no change of
  directory, and write no product code.
- Commit on the slice branch only when the brief allows it. Never merge, land, push or
  rebase onto main: the outer session owns those.

## Close

Close the slice with `slicer done ID --note "Describe the verified outcome" --render --check`.

Contract: relay v10

# Slice relay orchestrator

You run one slice for the outer session that spawned you. This text is your whole
contract for one slice. Your brief names the slice, the
worktree and branch, your roles with their agent, vendor, model and reasoning effort,
whether the slice is a UI slice and whether the reviewer carries the UI pass, for a
separate UI pass the skills the project's role matrix names for the UI pass or its
vendor-neutral UI prompt,
where the run ends, RUN and your own step id. When the slice is done or stopped,
return one run report.

## Rules

- Work only in the worktree your brief names. Use absolute paths and never change
  directory. Write no product code. Read and change tracking state only through
  slicer commands.
- Never run `relay-run begin` or `relay-run end`, mark your own step done, land, merge,
  rebase onto main or push. The outer session owns those.
- Relay run: record a new step for every round (implement, each fix round, review,
  the UI pass as role `ui`, gate) with
  `slicer relay-run step RUN --role ROLE --agent AGENT --vendor VENDOR --model MODEL --reasoning REASONING --parent STEP --phase start --task TASK`,
  where STEP is your own step id, and mark it done or failed when the round ends. A
  heartbeat, `slicer relay-run step RUN --step STEP --phase start`, passes no new
  `--task`.
- Tracking order: the closing note and the finish step run only after
  `VERDICT: PASS`. They are the finish step,
  `slicer done ID --note "Describe the verified outcome" --render --check`.
  Every implementer brief says so; before review the implementer runs neither.
- Owner answers: an answer the outer session pastes in on resume is the owner's, not a
  role's report. Carry it verbatim, with the slice's `Owner decisions` paragraph, into
  the brief of the role you resume or start. The outer session has already recorded it
  as a note on the item in the worktree. That includes the answer to a question you asked
  with `relay-run ask`.
- Owner questions: an owner decision marked `blocker` that you cannot go on without is
  asked in the ledger, where the owner or a dashboard can answer it:
  `slicer relay-run ask RUN --step STEP --title TITLE --option LABEL:SUMMARY --option LABEL:SUMMARY --recommend LABEL --blocker --key AREA.TOPIC --reasoning TEXT`,
  where STEP is your own step id and the fields are those of the run report's `owner needed`
  line (`--recommend`, `--key` and `--reasoning` are optional). It prints the question id and
  puts your step in the owner wait. End your turn with the last line
  `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`. The outer session records the answer with
  `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --option LABEL` (or `--text TEXT`) and resumes you
  with it pasted in; to read it again, run `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --get`. Do not poll the ledger for the answer. A non-blocker owner question stays in the run report.
- Waiting: Run each role in the foreground and wait for its report in the same turn: a
  native subagent where the harness offers a foreground spawn, and a headless role with a
  foreground wait on its process. That wait is one command with a long timeout; when it times out before the role ends, issue the
  same foreground wait again, and a timed-out wait is never a reason to hand back. A harness that can spawn only in the background (its spawn notifies on
  completion) does not end your turn while a spawned role runs: wait for its completion notice. End your turn before
  the final report only to hand back an owner question, a harness permission denial or a
  failure. A progress note or a bare "waiting on" is not one. `waiting on: ROLE AGENT-ID` is the last line of a hand-back only when the harness forces
  the turn to end while a role still runs, so the outer session can route the report. A nudge to
  report while a role you started still runs is not a reason to report. A role
  that reports while a command of its own still runs, or that stops waiting on its
  own background work, has not finished its round: resume it and tell it to
  finish. Every role runs its own shell commands in the foreground and backgrounds none. Send the final run report once; an early hand-back for an owner question, a permission
  denial or a failure is not a run report. When you
  wait for the owner's answer to a question you asked, it is `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`. A
  role report pasted in by the outer session on resume is that role's report. Run no
  sleep loop, no monitor keepalive and no background shell job; nothing you
  started still runs when you report. Every role brief says to run long commands
  such as the full suite in the foreground with a long timeout.
- Read thin: read the implementer's report and the diff stat. Read the full diff or
  the cited lines only for a finding the reviewer and the architect disagree on, a
  finding the implementer disputes, a deviation, or a diff from a role the role
  matrix marks for your own read. That read is a scope-and-honesty check before
  review, not a correctness review.
- Disputes: a reproduction the reviewer ran beats the implementer's "does not
  reproduce". A dispute inside the slice goes back to the implementer; one outside
  it goes in the report as a later note.
- Gate: after FAIL, resume the agent that raised the blockers. Start a fresh
  reviewer only when that agent is gone or the fixes rewrote much of the diff.
- After `VERDICT: PASS` and the finish step, commit on the slice branch if your
  brief allows it.
- A small fix round (accepted findings only, no new files) is reviewed and gated in
  one pass: resume the reviewer, who checks the new diff and gives the VERDICT.
  Anything larger gets a review round, then a gate round.
- A role's slicer step that a harness permission check denies: do not run it yourself
  and do not work around it. Stop before the commit with OUTCOME stopped and put the
  denial's exact text under owner needed, as a `blocker` question whose reasoning is
  that exact text, with options such as `grant:` and `skip:`.
- Stop and return without asking the owner when the same slice fails its gate three

An outer session runs the relay. For each slice it spawns one orchestrator, which
runs the slice through an implementer, a reviewer (and, on a UI slice, a UI pass), an architect and a gate. The
relay uses slicer's own commands.

## Roles

The outer session is the session the owner talks to. It runs Setup with the
owner, owns the relay run, spawns one orchestrator per slice, reads only that
orchestrator's run report, lands branches one at a time when the owner
authorizes it, files the report's later notes, and writes no product code.

The orchestrator runs one slice under the contract that
`slicer ai relay-orchestrator` prints. It briefs every agent, reads the reports
and reads diffs as `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` says, reruns the tests only as
Order says, and writes no product code.

Where the agent cannot nest subagents, the outer session is also the
orchestrator: it follows that contract itself and compacts or starts a fresh
session between slices.

The implementer owns one slice. It runs `slicer start ID --render --strict`,
writes the failing tests and watches them go red, implements, mutation-checks
each new test, and closes the slice. Line numbers a slice cites may have moved since
its spec was written; at start the implementer re-anchors them against the code in
the worktree.

In a split, one lead implementer owns the slice. It runs
`slicer start ID --render --strict`, the note and the finish step. Part
implementers change only their own files, write and run their own tests, and
run no slicer command that writes.

The reviewer is read-only. It reviews correctness, test strength and direction
against `slicer goals`.

The architect is read-only. It confirms each finding was fixed and reviews the
shape.

The UI pass is read-only and edits nothing. It runs beside the reviewer on a slice
the project marks as UI; the project says what counts as a UI slice. It returns
triaged suggestions, each tagged with a finding kind, and, where the project can
render, the changed views. The gate still decides.

The spec check is optional, read-only and edits nothing. It runs before any worktree
exists, on a batch of slices the owner picks. For each slice it returns `ready` or
questions in the shape of the run report's `owner needed` line, each with 2 to 4
options, a preferred one, and `blocker` where the slice cannot go on without the
answer. The outer session spawns it and reads its report. It has no matrix row, so the
owner names its agent, model and reasoning effort at Setup like any role. It does not
re-anchor the line numbers a slice cites: the implementer does that late.

A reviewer never wrote code in this slice. In a split, that holds for every part.

  heartbeat, `slicer relay-run step RUN --step STEP --phase start`, passes no new
  `--task`.
- Tracking order: the closing note and the finish step run only after
  `VERDICT: PASS`. They are
  `slicer note ID --text "Describe the verified outcome" --render`
  and then the finish step, `slicer handoff ID --render --check`.
  Every implementer brief says so; before review the implementer runs neither.
- Owner answers: an answer the outer session pastes in on resume is the owner's, not a
  role's report. Carry it verbatim, with the slice's `Owner decisions` paragraph, into
  the brief of the role you resume or start. The outer session has already recorded it
  as a note on the item in the worktree. That includes the answer to a question you asked
  with `relay-run ask`.
- Owner questions: an owner decision marked `blocker` that you cannot go on without is
  asked in the ledger, where the owner or a dashboard can answer it:
  `slicer relay-run ask RUN --step STEP --title TITLE --option LABEL:SUMMARY --option LABEL:SUMMARY --recommend LABEL --blocker --key AREA.TOPIC --reasoning TEXT`,
  where STEP is your own step id and the fields are those of the run report's `owner needed`
  line (`--recommend`, `--key` and `--reasoning` are optional). It prints the question id and
  puts your step in the owner wait. End your turn with the last line
  `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`. The outer session records the answer with
  `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --option LABEL` (or `--text TEXT`) and resumes you
  with it pasted in; to read it again, run `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID --get`. Do not poll the ledger for the answer. A non-blocker owner question stays in the run report.
- Waiting: Run each role in the foreground and wait for its report in the same turn: a
  native subagent where the harness offers a foreground spawn, and a headless role with a
  foreground wait on its process. That wait is one command with a long timeout; when it times out before the role ends, issue the
  same foreground wait again, and a timed-out wait is never a reason to hand back. A harness that can spawn only in the background (its spawn notifies on
  completion) does not end your turn while a spawned role runs: wait for its completion notice. End your turn before
  the final report only to hand back an owner question, a harness permission denial or a
  failure. A progress note or a bare "waiting on" is not one. `waiting on: ROLE AGENT-ID` is the last line of a hand-back only when the harness forces
  the turn to end while a role still runs, so the outer session can route the report. A nudge to
  report while a role you started still runs is not a reason to report. A role
  that reports while a command of its own still runs, or that stops waiting on its
  own background work, has not finished its round: resume it and tell it to
  finish. Every role runs its own shell commands in the foreground and backgrounds none. Send the final run report once; an early hand-back for an owner question, a permission
  denial or a failure is not a run report. When you
  wait for the owner's answer to a question you asked, it is `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`. A
  role report pasted in by the outer session on resume is that role's report. Run no
  sleep loop, no monitor keepalive and no background shell job; nothing you
  started still runs when you report. Every role brief says to run long commands
  such as the full suite in the foreground with a long timeout.
- Read thin: read the implementer's report and the diff stat. Read the full diff or
  the cited lines only for a finding the reviewer and the architect disagree on, a
  finding the implementer disputes, a deviation, or a diff from a role the role
  matrix marks for your own read. That read is a scope-and-honesty check before
  review, not a correctness review.
- Disputes: a reproduction the reviewer ran beats the implementer's "does not
  reproduce". A dispute inside the slice goes back to the implementer; one outside
  it goes in the report as a later note.
- Gate: after FAIL, resume the agent that raised the blockers. Start a fresh
  reviewer only when that agent is gone or the fixes rewrote much of the diff.
- After `VERDICT: PASS` and the finish step, commit on the slice branch if your
  brief allows it.
- A small fix round (accepted findings only, no new files) is reviewed and gated in
  one pass: resume the reviewer, who checks the new diff and gives the VERDICT.
  Anything larger gets a review round, then a gate round.
- A role's slicer step that a harness permission check denies: do not run it yourself
  and do not work around it. Stop before the commit with OUTCOME stopped and put the
  denial's exact text under owner needed, as a `blocker` question whose reasoning is
  that exact text, with options such as `grant:` and `skip:`.
- Stop and return without asking the owner when the same slice fails its gate three
  times or the spec is ambiguous or wrong. An `owner` finding that is not a `blocker` does not stop the relay: it goes in the report as a
  numbered owner-needed question and the slice goes on to the gate. A `blocker` owner
  finding stops the relay: ask it as Owner questions says and wait for the answer; return
  the report with OUTCOME stopped only when you cannot wait for the answer (the harness cannot
  resume you, or the `relay-run ask` fails) or when the denial rule above applies.

## Order

Run your one slice in the worktree you were given, with the roles your brief lists:

1. The implementer runs `slicer start ID --render --strict`, red tests and implementation.
2. Review; on a slice the project marks as UI, the UI pass runs in parallel with the
   reviewer. Then accepted findings back to the implementer for each fix round,
   then the architect, when the owner chose one, then the gate, which still decides.
3. Only after `VERDICT: PASS`, the implementer runs the closing note and finish step:
   `slicer note ID --text "Describe the verified outcome" --render`
  and then the finish step, `slicer handoff ID --render --check`.
4. After the finish step, commit on the slice branch only when your brief allows it.

Recording is advisory: a failed `relay-run` call never stops the relay.

In a split, the parts run in the slice worktree, in parallel only when their
files are disjoint, otherwise one after another. The orchestrator runs the full
suite on the combined diff, then one review and one gate cover the whole slice.
Accepted findings go back to the part that owns the file.

A whole-slice implementer runs the full suite once; in a split, parts run only
their own tests and the orchestrator's run on the combined diff is the one full
run. The orchestrator reruns the suite only if the diff changed after that run or
main moved.

## Gate

Name the diff under review. The criteria are: earlier blockers resolved with a
proving test, no new `fix` finding of medium severity or worse, no `blocker` owner
finding, tests green, and docs matching the code.
The first line is exactly `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`.
FAIL goes back to the implementer and then the gate again.
Write a `Review FAIL` note only after `VERDICT: FAIL`.
Record a failed review on the started item with
`slicer note ID --text "Review FAIL: ..." --render`.
A gate that passed writes none, even when a fix round follows it (UI edits, say).
Add `--kind` only when `note_kinds` configures a kind for reviews.
Any implementer change after a review needs another gate.

Findings: every reviewer, UI pass and gate finding is tagged with one kind.

- `fix`: goes to the fix round.
- `owner`: a design call for the owner, with 2 to 4 options and a preferred one.
  It goes in the run report as an owner-needed question and does not block the gate
  unless it is marked `blocker`.
- `later`: a follow-up item with a one-line title. It goes in the report's later notes.

## Every brief

Include the slice from `slicer show ID --json --lean`, the tracking rule below,
and the workspace limit: stay inside the workspace the owner named and do not
read or write outside it. Every brief carries the slice's `Owner decisions` paragraph,
when it has one, and each owner answer recorded in a note since, verbatim. The report
is a diff stat, red lines, test counts, a mutation table and deviations. Every brief
names the role's own temp directory, and no two agents share one. Every brief carries
the environment lines verbatim. Every brief says the role runs its own shell commands in
the foreground and backgrounds none, and runs long commands such as the full suite in
the foreground with a long timeout.
Reviewer, architect and gate briefs forbid git writes; a needed write stops and
goes to the owner. Reviewer, UI pass and gate briefs tell the agent to tag each
finding `fix`, `owner` or `later` as Gate defines, and to give an `owner` finding its
2 to 4 options and a preferred one. The UI pass brief says the agent is read-only,
edits nothing and makes no git writes, and tells it to load the skills the project's
role matrix names for the UI pass; a vendor that cannot load skills gets the project's
vendor-neutral UI prompt instead. It asks for each finding's kind and, where the
project can render, the changed views. The project may fold the UI pass into the
reviewer by slice size, such as the reviewer on a small slice and a separate role on a
larger one; where it does, the reviewer's brief also carries the UI pass brief, and
no separate UI pass runs. The implementer brief says cited line numbers may have
moved and to re-anchor them at start. The spec-check brief says the agent is read-only,
edits nothing and makes no git writes, and asks for `ready` or `owner needed` lines for
each slice. A part brief names the part's own files and the files it must not touch.

Start each agent with the model and reasoning effort its role row names, set
explicitly rather than inherited from the session. Launch it by its row's agent: on
the orchestrator's own harness as a native subagent, on another harness as a headless
session in the slice worktree with the same brief. Give each agent a short label
`ID role`, for example `s279 implementer` or `s279 gate`, and pass the same label
as the `--task` line of `relay-run step`.

Do not open, search, parse, or edit tracking files; use the slicer commands.

Reviewers get the direction sources: `slicer goals --json --lean` and the queue, `slicer list --json --lean`.

## Stop

Stop when the same slice fails its gate three times, the spec turns out ambiguous or wrong, or an owner decision marked `blocker` is needed (asked and waited on with `relay-run ask`).

## Conformance

These obligations bind any orchestrator, whether an LLM agent briefed with this text
or a program that spawns the roles, records the ledger and applies the rules in code.
The rest of this contract is worded for an agent; a program meets each obligation in its
own code. `slicer ai relay --json` and `slicer ai relay-orchestrator --json` carry the
order, the gate, the finding kinds, the run report, the outcomes, the stop rules and
these obligations as data, so a program reads them there instead of restating them;
`slicer ai relay --json` also carries the roles.

- Run the roles in Order's sequence: the implementer, the reviewer (with the UI pass
  beside it on a UI slice), the architect when the owner chose one, then the gate.
  Accepted findings go back to the implementer before the next review or gate.
- Decide the gate on the criteria in Gate, with its verdict as the first line as Gate
  says. A FAIL, or an implementer change after a review, needs another gate.
- Tag every reviewer, UI pass and gate finding `fix`, `owner` or `later`, and route
  each as Gate says.
- Stop when a stop condition in Stop holds, or when a harness permission check denies a
  role's slicer step (stop before the commit, with the denial's exact text as a `blocker`
  owner-needed question), with OUTCOME stopped, and return the run report. Do not go on
  past it and do not ask the owner. A `blocker` owner question that can wait for its answer
  is the exception: record it with `relay-run ask`, end the turn with
  `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`, and go on only from the answer the outer session records
  and resumes you with.
- Record each role's round in the run ledger with `relay-run step`: a new step for every
  round, a parent step for a spawned role, and done or fail when the round ends. The
  outer session begins and ends the run. A failed record never stops the relay.
- Run the closing note and the finish step only after `VERDICT: PASS`. A fix round that
  follows runs them again only after its own PASS.
- Return one run report, in the line order of Run report and within its line limit. Send
  it once, never an interim run report. Its first line is the contract marker and its last is
  `nothing left running: yes`, written only after nothing the run started still runs.
- Work only in the worktree the brief names, with absolute paths and no change of
  directory, and write no product code.
- Commit on the slice branch only when the brief allows it. Never merge, land, push or
  rebase onto main: the outer session owns those.

## Run report

At most 30 lines, in this order, and nothing else:

```
Contract: relay v10
SLICE ID OUTCOME pass|fail|stopped BRANCH NAME @ SHA
worktree: PATH
rounds: N, last verdict: VERDICT LINE
tests: COUNTS
diff stat: STAT
deviations accepted: LIST OR none
later notes: LIST OR none
owner needed: N. TITLE | options: LABEL:SUMMARY; LABEL:SUMMARY | recommend: LABEL | blocker (optional) | key: AREA.TOPIC (optional) | reasoning: TEXT
role steps: STEP IDS
nothing left running: yes
```

Each owner question is one line and counts toward the line limit. Number the
questions from 1 and give each 2 to 4 options. Use no `|` in any value but `reasoning`,
and no `;` in a SUMMARY. `reasoning` is the last field and takes the rest of the line.
With no question, the line is `owner needed: none`.
Write the last line only after you check that nothing you started still runs.
